summary: Saskatchewan fire tower known only from a website listing of its coordinates; the lake it shares a name with lies 41 km NNE of La Loche.

evidence.supports: Listing gives Tocker Lake tower's coordinates as 56 degrees 48 minutes 09.3 seconds N, 109 degrees 07 minutes 48.6 seconds W
Listing heading names the tower Tocker Lake
Tocker Lake is a small lake in central Saskatchewan, 41 km NNE of La Loche
evidence.quote: Tocker Lake is a small lake in central Saskatchewan. It is located 41km NNE of La Loche.

evidence.supports: The lake is named after Harry Ronald Tocker
evidence.quote: Tocker Lake is named after Harry Ronald Tocker.

evidence.supports: Department of Natural Resources began building towers at about fifty-mile intervals across northern Saskatchewan
evidence.quote: The Department of Natural Resources soon began constructing fire control towers at approximately fifty-mile intervals across northern Saskatchewan.

evidence.supports: Spacing chosen so that towermen could reach each other by radio
evidence.quote: This distance was chosen to assure that radio contact could be made between tower men.

evidence.supports: Towers of this kind carried a fire finder, a two-way radio and field glasses
evidence.quote: The equipment in the tower, as in all other towers, consisted of a fire finder, two-way radio, and a pair of field glasses.

sources.title: Towers and Saskatchewan Environment - Big River and Area

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The coordinates match the listing (56-48-09.3 X 109-07-48.6 is 56.80258, -109.13017). SaskLakes (cite 2) describes the lake, not the tower, so the story does not place the tower relative to the lake beyond the shared name. No build date, height, status or fate for the tower appears in any page read. The record's agency and staffing note are unsourced in pages read. Two searches found no tower-specific history. The Big River history (cite 3) is provincial background, not a source on this site.
